concept.name: Evening doji star
concept.definition: A three-candlestick top reversal pattern: a long white body is followed by a doji that gaps above it (the doji star), and then a long black body that closes well into the first candle's real body. It is the evening star with a doji as the middle candle, conventionally regarded as a stronger bearish signal because the doji marks a more complete stall in buying.
concept.intuition: After heavy buying, the market gaps up but freezes dead flat (a doji), then sellers drive price deep back into the prior gains; the motionless middle candle shows buyers are exhausted.
concept.mechanics: From OHLC data: candle 1 is a long white body in an uptrend; candle 2 is a doji whose body (and classically whose range) sits above body 1; candle 3 is a long black body closing below the midpoint of body 1. When the doji's shadows also gap clear of both neighbors, the pattern becomes the rarer bearish abandoned baby.
concept.failure_modes: Strict gap requirements make genuine instances rare in forex and crypto, and relaxed matches are much less reliable. Strong uptrends often shrug off the pattern after one down candle.
concept.misconceptions: It is not the same as a plain evening star; the star must be a doji. Nor is it a bearish abandoned baby, which additionally requires the doji's full shadow range to be separated by gaps from both neighbors.
concept.example: A stock rallies with a long white candle (80.00 to 83.00), gaps up into a doji near 83.40, then prints a long black candle closing at 80.80. The evening doji star is read as a strong top reversal signal.
